items.title: ‘Ramy’s Ramy Youssef & Steve Way Reteaming On Disability-Themed Body Swap Comedy
items.summary:
Ramy Youssef and Steve Way, who worked together on the Hulu comedy Ramy, are teaming up again on a feature film built around a body swap between a man with muscular dystrophy and his caregiver. Way will star and co-write the untitled project with Jon Braylock, a longtime friend and collaborator of both men. Youssef is producing through his Cairo Cowboy banner.

Deadline reported that the premise follows Way's character, who has muscular dystrophy, trading bodies with his burly caregiver. Way and Braylock are producing alongside Youssef, with Inevitable Studios and Give Not Take Media also on the producing team.

Way, who was born with congenital muscular dystrophy, has spoken publicly about the condition since he was 10, including through his work with the Muscular Dystrophy Association. Beyond Ramy, he recently drew strong reviews for a supporting role opposite Emmy Rossum and Lola Petticrew in Elizabeth Meriwether's Hulu series Furious, which Hulu has renewed for a second season.

Braylock co-created and starred in Netflix's Astronomy Club: The Sketch Show, and his writing credits include Golden Axe, Ted: The Animated Series, Grown-ish and The G Word With Adam Conover. He also co-hosts the podcast Black Men Can't Jump in Hollywood.

The two production companies attached both work in this territory by design. Inevitable Studios is the production arm of the Inevitable Foundation, co-founded by Richie Siegel and Marisa Torelli-Pedevska, and focuses on film and television told through a disability lens. Give Not Take Media, owned by the national advocacy organization Caring Across Generations, develops projects about caregiving, disability and aging.

Youssef, who won a Golden Globe for Ramy and released his third HBO stand-up special, Ramy Youssef: In Love, in April, is currently in production on his feature directorial debut, Martha and Muhammad, for A24. He stars in that film opposite Sharon Stone.

items.title: Garth Brooks Buying Spot on Nashville Radio Dial to Create a New Country Station, With a Promise to Give Female Artists a More Prominent Shot
items.summary:
Garth Brooks is buying a spot on the Nashville FM dial. His company, Sevens Network, LLC, has agreed to purchase the 100.1 FM frequency currently occupied by the adult-alternative station Lightning 100, WRLT-FM, and turn it into a new country station mixing established names with younger artists.

Variety reported that the seller is Tuned In Broadcasting and that the deal still requires FCC approval. Lightning 100, a Nashville fixture for decades, is not going away: once the sale closes, it moves to Cromwell Media's 106.3 FM and 102.5 FM HD3 frequencies with its triple-A format intact. Until then it keeps broadcasting from 100.1.

Brooks says the new station, FM-100, will prioritize local listeners over industry metrics, and will not report airplay to the trades. "Our job is NOT to compete with the local channels in Nashville, but to PROMOTE what they have going on," he said in a statement. "We are NOT a reporter; we are a SERVICE to Music City and its businesses."

A stated centerpiece of the format is female artists, who have long received far less country radio airplay than men. A statement on Brooks' website said the station has an opportunity to feature women from the 1960s through the present alongside one another. "We NEED both sides telling the story of country music," Brooks said. "That includes spotlighting female artists going back to the 60s as well as active in the present day."

The idea came from a misunderstanding. Brooks said he saw a Lightning 100 social media post reading "Save Our Station" in 2025 and assumed it was current, when it actually dated to the COVID era roughly six years earlier. "A country artist buying an indie-rock station made no sense," he said, but buying the dial position while the station relocated nearby solved both problems.

Brooks also pointed to pre-recorded national programming leaving Nashville residents without live local information during emergencies, and framed FM-100 as a place to get real-time updates from people rather than automation. He described a longer-term ambition of a 24-hour global station, while saying the initial focus is on serving Nashville itself.

items.title: Ecco2k Sets New Album Echo
items.summary:
Ecco2k has announced his second solo album. Echo arrives Thursday, November 12 on the rapper-producer's own label, 9th, seven years after his debut solo record, E.

The 12-track album includes the previously released songs "Aldehydes and Ketones" and "Sky Burial" alongside 10 new ones. As Pitchfork reported, Echo contains no guest features, and Ecco2k — whose real name is Zak Arogundade — produced every track himself or with regular collaborators Gud, Whitearmor, Felix Lee and Mechatok.

Press materials describe the record as following "a vagabond character who wanders the world carrying a broadcast antenna and a crown of flowers." The character moves alone through mountains, deserts, beaches, cities and villages, "searching for signals in a world of overwhelming beauty and indifference, listening and transmitting."

Arogundade first drew attention as part of Drain Gang, the Swedish collective that also includes Bladee, Thaiboy Digital and Whitearmor. The group has released two albums, D&G in 2017 and Trash Island in 2019. Arogundade and Bladee also released a joint album, Crest, in 2022.

The full tracklist runs: "Aldehydes and Ketones," "Echo," "Industrial Strength," "Fæmous Vagrant," "Plume," "Cuban Heel," "French Exit," "Loveless Animal, Lawless Criminal," "Encore," "Held Overnight," "Swimming in Fountains" and "Sky Burial."
